title: Why Africa's Borders Are Straight Lines (It's Not What You Think)
hook: In the winter of 1884, fourteen delegations sat around a map of Africa in Berlin. Not one of them was African. Thirty years later, almost 90% of the continent belonged to Europe.
summary: But did they really draw Africa's borders with a ruler? The real story is stranger than you think. In this video we follow the Scramble for Africa: Bismarck's Berlin Conference, the myth most people believe, the straight lines drawn along latitude and longitude, the bizarre Caprivi Strip that led straight to a waterfall, and the choice African leaders made in 1964 to keep borders they never chose.
sources: General Act of the Berlin Conference (1885)
Organisation of African Unity, Cairo Resolution on border disputes (1964)
